correctness.rationale: The exact absence-indicator covariance formula yields both models. Exhaustive integer partitions for every \(N\le6\) and all sample depths establish a unique first two-switch profile \((4,1,1)\), verified independently by 270 exact direct-outcome variance computations. At depths 2,3,4 the signs are respectively negative, positive, negative. For all integers \(t\ge2\) the \((2t,1,\ldots,1)\) family has explicitly negative depth-two difference, positive depth-three difference by an all-positive polynomial in t-2, and negative full-census difference because one design is deterministic while the other is nondegenerate. Finite testing is supplemental to that analytic proof.

value.rationale: The variance question is motivated by choosing or interpreting two standard ecological sampling models at equal depth. Unlike a linear statistic with ordinary finite-population variance reduction, observed richness counts categories nonlinearly. The first sharp and unique reentrant variance-order profile, together with all-size exact witnesses, identifies a structural failure of a common uncertainty comparison, not an arbitrary numerical slice or a change of notation. There is no assertion that this determines confidence intervals for estimated true richness, spatially correlated samples, or the maximal number of switches for general larger censuses.
